summary: Attacked the extraction of Temkin, 'Tame distillation and desingularization by p-alterations' (Ann. of Math. 186 (2017) 97–126; arXiv:1508.06255v2): 64 items, 3 routes and 4 source issues. There are seventeen findings, ten medium and seven low. The statements, locators, the four library citations and E1–E4 hold. Two findings concern the paper's mathematics. First, Temkin's definition of universal P-resolvability (§4.1.4) drops the projectivity that his source (Exposé X §3.3.3) has, so §4.3.2 does not give the projective b of Theorem 1.2.5. The review's added note, which derives it from Theorem 4.3.1(ii), is refuted by an explicit counterexample. Second, Step 4 of Theorem 4.2.1 does not give a separable alteration in the separable case, which Theorem 4.3.1(iii) needs; a repair via separably P-closed fields is given. Three unrecorded mistakes are low: the minimal-polynomial step of Lemma 3.2.10 (with a counterexample), the false 'only if' of §3.1.7 (with a counterexample), and misprints in Lemma 3.2.10 and Step 10. The other medium findings concern statuses and owners. L5's 'planned' flattening, normalization and semistable-curve items are in the wrong generality. SF.4 already owns flattening and proved resolution settings. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1 and LocalFieldsRamification Layer 4 plan wild inertia as a pro-p Sylow subgroup. Tau Ceti ModularCurves 4D owns strict henselisation. H1:henselian and C5 plan Huber's Zariski–Riemann limit. Tau Ceti's Spv and Mathlib's coarsenings and linear disjointness make parts of three 'missing' items library. No items cover qe or universally Japanese schemes, regular schemes, snc divisors or finite quotients, nor Step 10's Abhyankar lemma, Kato's Theorem 8.2 and log smoothness of semistable curves.
checked: The source, re-fetched on 29 September 2026: the Annals PDF https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v186-n1-p03-p.pdf has SHA-256 1f4ac06f2f31430abdd984d8e635a324defb6de340f6a599f708c04996fbfba4, and arXiv:1508.06255v2 has SHA-256 24f67ac306b7af4bf058c086a76f29bbd8854639354bcb241275d8e2dd43a435. Both are the recorded hashes. The arXiv listing shows v2 (21 February 2017) as the last version. Both texts were read completely, §§1–4 and the references, and every new finding's quotation was located in both. Page images at 200 dpi of pp. 117 and 123 were checked for the quoted misprints.

Every numbered statement from Theorem 1.2.5 to Remark 4.3.4 against the 64 items: statement, hypotheses, locator. Counts: 4 library, 5 planned, 55 missing; routes 26 + 27 + 2 = 55, each missing id routed exactly once. Statements hold except the notation in henselian-ramification (finding 16).

E1–E4 at their locators. E1: the gap is real. Example: S = Spec ℤ (universally P-resolvable for every P, by normalization), X = A¹ over ℤ[1/2], and P = the odd primes, so char(X) ⊆ P. If the separable alteration of Step 3, or its allowed enlargement, is Spec ℤ[i] → Spec ℤ, which is wild at 2, then Theorem 3.3.6 yields a {2}-alteration of degree > 1, not a P-alteration. Only the review's description of Exposé X is off (finding 14). E2, E3, E4: confirmed. For E4, the p_i = 1 branch is reachable, and the corrected reading works.

The review's changes: the four verdicts, E4, the note on lemma-2-6-3-ii (correct) and the note on theorem-1-2-5. The theorem-1-2-5 note is wrong: 4.3.1(ii) does not give b⁻¹(Z) snc, by an explicit counterexample (finding 1).

Illusie–Temkin, Exposé X, in arXiv:1207.3648v1: §3.3.1–3.3.3 (definitions of alterations and universal resolvability), Theorem 3.4 and its Steps 4–10, Remark 3.4.1 and the proof of Theorem 3.5. They were read to check Temkin's claims about [IT14b] (findings 1, 2, 3, 14). The Cossart–Piltant arXiv:1412.0868 abstract and listing, and the Crossref record of its 2019 publication, were also read (finding 15).

The missing statuses, by searching the pinned declarations index (both libraries) and opening the files. Searches: henselization (none); Prüfer (none); LinearDisjoint (found, finding 8); LocalSubring (found, finding 11); ValuationSubring.ofPrime and idealOfLE (found, finding 8); ValuationSpectrum, SpectralSpace and constructible topology (found, findings 8 and 11); Chevalley and isConstructible_image (found, finding 11); generalizingMap and UniversallyOpen (found, finding 11); tame and purely wild (none); Riemann–Zariski and alteration (none); Excellent, Japanese and Nagata (none); regular local rings and normal crossings (none); Abhyankar and rational rank (none); SchurZassenhaus (finite only); HenselianLocalRing and TauCeti.henselianLocalRing_integer (local fields only); Valuation.HasExtension.

The planned statuses, against the full stage text: AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5 (tasks 1–5; finding 3) and CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra (Kato's chart criterion holds; log regularity, Abhyankar and Kato 8.2 are not in it, finding 10).

Routes: route 1 has the same id, title, parent and area as the DITTMANN-POP and JANNSEN proposals. Route 2's title reproduces the Tau Ceti parent's. Route 3's stage id resolves. The brief texts were checked against the item list and the atlas (findings 3–7, 9, 10, 17).

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-TEMKIN-17.result.json: the note on item PAPER-TEMKIN-17/theorem-1-2-5 (added by REV-PAPER-TEMKIN-17), item PAPER-TEMKIN-17/universal-p-resolvability, and sourceIssues (no entry)
findings.claim: Theorem 1.2.5 claims a projective char(X)-alteration b with b⁻¹(Z) snc. §4.3.2 derives it from Theorem 4.3.1(i), but Temkin's §4.1.4 defines universal P-resolvability without projectivity, so (i) gives no projective b. The item universal-p-resolvability copies that definition, and no source issue records the omission. The review's added note says the projective b 'comes from Theorem 4.3.1(ii)' and that 'the blueprint should derive the first claim from (ii)'. That derivation does not work. (ii) controls only Z′ = b⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′), not b⁻¹(Z), and b⁻¹(Z) need not even be a divisor. The review's change thus replaces one unsupported derivation with another. The omission is Temkin's: the definition he adapts, Illusie–Temkin Exposé X §3.3.3, requires the resolving morphism to be projective.
findings.evidence: Temkin, Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §4.1.4, p. 121 (same in arXiv v2, p. 21): 'Assume that for any alteration Y → X and a nowhere dense closed subset Z ⊂ Y, there exists a P-alteration f : Y′ → Y such that Y′ is regular and Z′ = f⁻¹(Z) is an snc divisor. Then we say that X is universally P-resolvable.' No projectivity. §4.3.2, p. 124: 'Theorem 4.3.1(i) implies that X is universally char(X)-resolvable. This proves the first claim of Theorem 1.2.5.' Illusie–Temkin, Exposé X, §3.3.3, p. 159 of arXiv:1207.3648v1: 'Assume that for any alteration Y → X and nowhere dense closed subset Z ⊂ Y there exists a surjective projective morphism f : Y′ → Y such that Y′ is regular and Z′ = f⁻¹(Z) is an snc divisor. … If, furthermore, one can always choose such f to be … l′-alteration … then we say that X is … universally l′-resolvable.' The (ii) route fails by a counterexample. Let S = X be a regular excellent surface (for example Spec of a regular two-dimensional excellent local ring, universally P-resolvable by Lipman for every P ⊇ char(S)), f = id, and Z = V(x, y) a closed point with x, y a regular system of parameters. Take a = b = f′ = id, W′ = V(xy) and Z′ = V(xy). Then a and b are projective P-alterations of degree 1 with regular sources, f′ is pseudo-projective, W′ and Z′ are snc, Z′ = b⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′) because the point lies on V(xy), and (X′, Z′) → (S′, W′) is the identity, which is log smooth. Every conclusion of 4.3.1(ii) holds, yet b⁻¹(Z) is a point, not an snc divisor. So (ii) as stated does not yield 'b⁻¹(Z) is an snc divisor'. (Exposé X's own sentence '(i) follows from (ii)', p. 162, has the same shape; the blueprint must take the snc condition on b⁻¹(Z) from the proof, not from the statement of (ii).)
findings.fix: (1) Add sourceIssues entry E5, kind 'gap', locator '§4.1.4, p. 121, and §4.3.2, p. 124 (arXiv v2, pp. 21, 23)', affects 'the proof' (of Theorem 1.2.5's projectivity claim), known 'Illusie–Temkin, Exposé X, §3.3.3 (the definition Temkin adapts) requires f surjective and projective'. Correction: 'In §4.1.4, f : Y′ → Y is a projective P-alteration, as in Exposé X, §3.3.3; the proof of Theorem 4.3.1(i), copied from Exposé X, Theorem 3.5, produces projective alterations.' (2) Restate item universal-p-resolvability with 'a projective P-alteration f'. (3) Replace the review's note on theorem-1-2-5 by: 'Projectivity comes from the projective form of universal P-resolvability (E5) through Theorem 4.3.1(i). It does not follow from 4.3.1(ii), which controls only b⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′). The blueprint must prove that the construction behind (ii) can be arranged so that b⁻¹(Z) itself is snc.' (4) Put the same statement of universal resolvability into the PrimeToDegreeAlterations brief.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-TEMKIN-17.result.json: sourceIssues (no entry); items PAPER-TEMKIN-17/theorem-4-2-1, theorem-3-3-6, theorem-3-2-12; the PrimeToDegreeAlterations brief
findings.claim: The separable case of Theorem 4.2.1 has an unrecorded gap in Step 4. In the 'resp.' case the base is universally separably P-resolvable and a must be a separable P-alteration. Step 4 obtains a : S′ → S from Theorem 3.3.6, which asserts only a P-alteration X′ → X. Its source, Theorem 3.2.12, takes K′ inside an arbitrary maximal P-extension K̄ of K. When char K = p ∈ P, K̄ contains K^{1/p^∞}, and nothing makes the chosen finite subextensions K_x separable. So a need not be separable. The separable case is what the proof of Theorem 4.3.1(iii) needs. That proof copies Exposé X, Theorem 3.5, whose induction applies Theorem 3.4 over a base Y of positive characteristic that is 'universally separably l′-resolvable'. So the gap reaches the separability claims of Theorems 1.2.5, 1.2.9(ii) and 4.3.1(iii). Gabber's Sylow step has no such problem: S̄/G_ℓ → S is automatically separable when S̄ → S is. Neither the extraction nor the review records this.
findings.evidence: Temkin, Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), Theorem 4.2.1, p. 121: 'Assume that S is universally P-resolvable (resp. universally separably P-resolvable) … Then there exist a projective P-alteration (resp. a separable projective P-alteration) a : S′ → S'. Step 4, p. 122: 'By Theorem 3.3.6, enlarging a we can achieve that it factors into a composition of a tame Galois covering S̄ → S′ and a P-alteration a : S′ → S.' Theorem 3.3.6, p. 120: '… factors into a composition of a tame Galois covering Y′ → X′ and a P-alteration X′ → X' (no separability). Theorem 3.2.12, p. 118: 'if K̄/K is an arbitrary P-maximal extension, then one can achieve that K′ ⊆ K̄'. Its proof fixes 'a maximal P-extension K̄/K' and needs it P-closed, to apply Lemma 3.2.5. Exposé X, proof of Theorem 3.5 (arXiv:1207.3648v1, p. 164): 'Y is universally separably l′-resolvable by the induction assumption', where Theorem 3.4 is applied over Y. Same text in arXiv:1508.06255v2, pp. 18–22.
findings.fix: Add sourceIssues entry E6, kind 'gap', locator 'Theorem 4.2.1, Step 4, p. 122, in the separable case; Theorems 3.2.12 and 3.3.6', affects 'the proof', known 'new'. Correction: prove separable variants of Theorems 3.2.12 and 3.3.6, with K̄ a maximal separable P-extension. The one new input is that a separably P-closed field K is separably P-tame. Proof: its perfection K^{perf} is P-closed, since a finite separable extension of K^{perf} of degree d descends by Frobenius twisting of the minimal polynomial to a separable extension of K of degree d. So K^{perf} is P-tame by Lemma 3.2.5. Because (K^{perf})^t = K^t K^{perf} (as in the proof of Theorem 2.5.5) and K^t K^{perf} ∩ K^s = K^t, a separable l/K is tame exactly when lK^{perf}/K^{perf} is. The rest of the proofs of 3.2.12 and 3.3.6 is unchanged, and then Step 4 gives a separable P-alteration. Add the separable variants as items routed with theorem-3-3-6, and add E6 to the note of theorem-4-2-1 and to the PrimeToDegreeAlterations brief.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-TEMKIN-17.result.json: items PAPER-TEMKIN-17/flattening, PAPER-TEMKIN-17/normalization-japanese and PAPER-TEMKIN-17/semistable-curve-alteration (status 'planned' at AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5), and route 1's brief ('Import … flattening, normalization and semistable curve reduction from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5')
findings.claim:
L5 plans these only in the generality of de Jong's field and valuation-base cases, for finite-type schemes. Temkin needs more:
- **Flattening:** Raynaud–Gruson for a finite-type, not necessarily finitely presented, morphism over an arbitrary qcqs tight modification X_i (Lemma 3.1.6, citing Stacks 081R).
- **Normalization:** finiteness of normalization over an arbitrary noetherian universally Japanese integral scheme (Lemma 3.3.4, Theorem 3.3.6).
- **Semistable curves:** semistable reduction of multipointed curves over an arbitrary noetherian qe normal base S after a separable alteration (Theorem 4.2.1, Steps 1–3). Exposé X says this needs Temkin's stable modification theorem, not de Jong's result.
So 'planned' overstates the plan. Since the brief imports all three from L5, the general forms have no owner.
findings.evidence: research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons.json, stage L5: 'Prove the forms of de Jong … Theorems 4.1 and 6.5 used by the comparison proof: alteration to a smooth situation with normal-crossing boundary in the field case and the semistable alteration situation over the valuation base' and task 1 'Establish the required finite-type scheme geometry: normalization under the applicable excellence hypotheses, flattening by blowup, strict transforms'. Temkin, proof of Lemma 3.1.6, p. 115: 'One cannot use [RG71, Th. 5.7.9] directly since f does not have to be of finite presentation, but [St, tag 081R] extends the claim to the case we need'; there X_i is any tight modification of an arbitrary qcqs pointed scheme. Lemma 3.3.4 and Theorem 3.3.6, pp. 119–120: 'X is a noetherian universally Japanese integral scheme'. Theorem 4.2.1, p. 122: 'Steps 1–2 of [IT14b, Th. 3.4] extend verbatim … Then Step 3 produces … (X̄, Z̄_h) is a semistable multipointed S̄-curve', for S any noetherian qe scheme. Exposé X, Remark 3.4.1(i) (arXiv:1207.3648v1, p. 162): 'One considers non-proper relative curves in 3.4, and this is the only point that requires to use the stable modification theorem instead of de Jong's result.'
findings.fix: Change the three items to 'missing'. Where L5 plans the finite-type special case, keep it as the base case in the note. Route the general forms: flattening over qcqs schemes (Stacks 081R), and normalization over noetherian universally Japanese schemes, to the owner fixed in finding 4 (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4), or to PrimeToDegreeAlterations if the maintainer prefers. Route the stable modification of multipointed relative curves over a noetherian qe normal base (the stable modification theorem of Temkin, Stable modification of relative curves, J. Algebraic Geom. 19 (2010), which Exposé X Remark 3.4.1(i) names; Step 5 also cites its §1.6) to PrimeToDegreeAlterations, and extend the Tem10 prerequisite entry's 'why' to cover it. Amend route 1's import sentence accordingly.

- **MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles** requests Raynaud–Gruson flattening and resolution in named proved settings from SF.4.

findings.claim:
Route 2 says the Krull-valued ramification theory 'has no owner' and that LocalFieldsRamification plans 'Layers 2–3' only. Both claims are wrong for §2.2.6.
- **ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles** plans, in its stage text, the 'valuation-theoretic pro-p Sylow/tame comparison' for valuation rings of arbitrary rank. That is Temkin's §2.2.6 over k^u: W_k is the pro-p Sylow subgroup of inertia, and Gal(k^t/k^u) = Hom(|(k^t)^×|/|k^×|, μ). Its draft packet has nodes for exactly this and for the strict henselization of a valuation ring (Temkin's (k^u)° = (k°)^sh).
- **Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layer 4**, not Layers 2–3, plans wild inertia as the pro-p Sylow subgroup of inertia and the tame quotient, for local fields.
- **ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 2**, the Tau Ceti roadmap Layer 4 consumes, owns profinite Sylow theory.
The brief imports none of them. Two roadmaps would plan the same wild-inertia theorem, and the Part II would restate profinite Sylow theory.

findings.claim:
The review's reason says nothing in the atlas owns Riemann–Zariski spaces of schemes, because 'DiamondEtaleCohomology:C5's Zariski–Riemann models are for strictly totally disconnected spaces'. That misreads the atlas. Two stages already plan Huber's Zariski–Riemann limit theorem:
- **ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian** plans the 'Zariski–Riemann argument'. Its draft packet has a node stating Huber 1993, Lemma 2.1: {V ∈ Spv K : s(A) ⊆ V} ≅ lim |X| over projective integral A-models with dominant K-point.
- **DiamondEtaleCohomology:C5** says it will 'Construct the Zariski–Riemann models and their limit/cohomology comparisons'.
Huber's lemma is Temkin's Lemma 3.1.3 for X = Spec A and a dominant point. Temkin's RZ_K(X) generalizes it to qcqs X, proper modifications and non-dominant points. Under PROTOCOL §15 the general construction must cite that special case and prove itself compatible with it. The extraction's notes cite only AdicSpaces Layer 1.

findings.claim:
Step 10 of Theorem 4.2.1 uses three log-geometric theorems that are neither items nor planned anywhere:
- **Abhyankar's lemma in log form.** Let S be regular with snc W and S̄ its tame Galois covering, normal and étale over S ∖ W. Then (S̄, W̄) → (S, W) is Kummer étale and (S̄, W̄) is log regular (Grothendieck–Murre; SGA 1 XIII §5).
- **Kato's theorem.** A log smooth log scheme over a log regular base is log regular (Kato, Toric singularities, Theorem 8.2).
- **Semistable curves are log smooth.** A semistable multipointed curve, with the log structure of its boundary, is log smooth over the base.
CR.5 plans 'Kummer and log-smooth morphisms' as definitions only. The Abhyankar-lemma arguments elsewhere in the atlas (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.5, AlgebraicCurves Layer 8) are for a smooth codimension-one locus or for function fields.

findings.claim: The proof of Lemma 3.2.10, unramified case, asserts that the polynomial f from Chevalley's theorem is 'the minimal polynomial of a over K'. Chevalley's theorem does not give that, and without it the claimed injectivity of A → L fails. Lemma 2.3.4 then does not apply to A, which is not a subring of L. The conclusion survives: replace f by the minimal polynomial g of a. The review says it checked §§2–3 line by line; the gap is not recorded.
findings.evidence: Temkin, proof of Lemma 3.2.10, p. 117 (page image checked; same in arXiv v2, p. 17): 'O_y is a localization of a ring O_x[t]/(f(t)) such that f(t) is monic and … f′(a) ∈ O_y^× … We claim that the homomorphism A → L taking t to a is injective. … The latter follows from the facts that O_x′ is integrally closed and f(t) is the minimal polynomial of a over K.' Counterexample to the unstated step: K = L = ℚ, O_x = O_y = ℤ_(p), a = 0, f(t) = t(t − 1). Then O_x[t]/(f) ≅ ℤ_(p) × ℤ_(p), and its localization at the prime of the first factor is O_y = ℤ_(p), with t ↦ a = 0 and f′(0) = −1 a unit. So (O_y, f, a) is as Chevalley's theorem provides. But f is not the minimal polynomial t of 0, and A = ℤ_(p)[t, f′(t)⁻¹]/(f) ≅ ℤ_(p) × ℤ_(p) → ℚ, t ↦ 0, kills (0, 1): it is not injective. Repair: g := minpoly_K(a) ∈ O_x[t], since O_x is integrally closed and a is integral. Gauss's lemma gives f = gh in O_x[t]. From f′(a) = g′(a)h(a) ∈ O_y^×, both g′(a) and h(a) are units, so O_y is also a localization of O_x[t]/(g), and the printed argument runs with g.

Correction: 'Replace f by the minimal polynomial g of a over K: g ∈ O_x[t], g divides f, and g′(a), h(a) ∈ O_y^× where f = gh, so O_y is a localization of O_x[t]/(g) with g′(a) a unit; then A = O_x′[t, g′(t)⁻¹]/(g) embeds in L.' findings.claim: E1's review reason says that in Exposé X, Theorem 3.4 'the Sylow trick needed tameness only over X, so char(X) ⊆ {ℓ}′ sufficed there'. But Exposé X's hypothesis already includes ℓ invertible on S. It defines universal ℓ′-resolvability only 'for a prime l invertible on X', and Theorem 3.4 assumes S universally ℓ′-resolvable, so char(S) ⊆ {ℓ}′ there. Temkin's 'The particular case of the theorem when P = {l}′ is [IT14b, Th. 3.4]' is therefore true only under char(S) ⊆ P. His char(X) ⊆ P version is strictly more general than its source. This supports E1's first repair, char(S) ⊆ P, which is literally Exposé X's hypothesis. The record should say so.
